findings.title: Routine cleanup progress logged at Error level on every cycle
findings.body: The new cleanup code logs normal, healthy operation with r.log.Error at six sites: lines 534, 537 ("Annotations to clean by time" / "cleaned annotations by time"), 554, 557 (count variants), and 576, 579 ("Tags to clean" / "cleaned tags"). These fire on every cleanup run even when there is nothing to delete (count=0), include the full ID list (up to AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize entries, e.g. tens of thousands), and carry a nil "err" key. Combined with the cleanup ticker being changed to every minute in cleanup.go, this produces a constant stream of ERROR log lines per Grafana instance in the healthy case, which will break error-rate-based alerting/monitoring and inflate log volume. These look like debugging leftovers and should be Debug level (and probably not log raw ID slices).

findings.title: Cleanup ticker changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute for all jobs
findings.body: The PR, which is scoped to the annotation cleanup deadlock, changes the CleanUpService ticker from 10 minutes to 1 minute. This makes every cleanup job run 10x more often on every Grafana instance: deleting expired snapshots, dashboard versions, images, user invites, short URLs, query history rows (including the two EnforceRowLimit queries), scanning/removing temp files, plus the annotation cleanup itself. That is a significant, undocumented increase in background DB and disk load, and it also increases how often annotation deletes race with annotation inserts — the exact contention this PR is trying to defuse. If this is intentional it needs justification in the PR and ideally a config option; if it is a leftover from local deadlock reproduction, it should be reverted.

findings.title: deleteByIDs only guards SQLite's parameter limit; oversized batch sizes fail on Postgres/MySQL
findings.body: deleteByIDs builds DELETE FROM ... WHERE id IN (?, ?, ...) with one bind parameter per ID and only switches away from parameters for SQLite when AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > 999. On other databases the batch size is configurable and unvalidated: if it is set above the driver's bind-parameter cap (65535 for Postgres, and MySQL prepared statements have a similar 65535 placeholder limit), every cleanup batch will fail with a parameter-count error, so cleanup never makes progress. The previous subquery-based DELETE had no parameter list at all, so this is a regression for large configured batch sizes. Consider chunking the ID slice to a safe per-statement size (e.g. 1000) for all dialects.

findings.title: SQLite inline-ID path builds SQL with quadratic string copying
findings.body: In the SQLite branch of deleteByIDs the ID list is built with `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)` in a loop, which copies the entire accumulated string on every iteration — O(n^2) work. With the batch size this path is designed for (e.g. 32767 IDs, as exercised by the new test), that is on the order of gigabytes of byte copying per batch, repeated on every cleanup cycle while a backlog exists. Using a strings.Builder with strconv.AppendInt (or strings.Join on pre-formatted values) would make it linear.
